key_insight: Weekly blood microsampling detected higher interferon-related gene signatures before and during dermatomyositis flares, suggesting a potential early molecular flare signal.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could support earlier flare detection in dermatomyositis using minimally invasive home-collected blood samples.
method: Six women with dermatomyositis were followed for 6 months with weekly patient-reported disease activity scoring.
Patients self-collected weekly 125 µL blood microsamples that were shipped for RNA sequencing.
Transcriptomic analyses assessed interferon scores, differential gene expression, and pathway enrichment around flare events.
evidence_signal: In this feasibility study of 6 patients and 54 RNA-seq samples across 9 timepoints, interferon scores were significantly higher in flare-associated samples, with enrichment of interferon-related gene sets in pre-flare and flare samples.
watch_item: Very small sample size and feasibility design mean the flare signal needs larger, independent validation before it can be used in practice.
paper_title: Longitudinal interferon signatures are associated with disease flare in dermatomyositis
